- Elevates risk of adult respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [Excessive IV crystalloid or colloid solutions should be avoided because they cause haemodilution, increase coagulopathy and increase the risk of adult respiratory distress syndrome.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Contrast the primary objectives of Early Total Care (ETC) and Damage Control Surgery (DCS).
back:
- ETC: Definitive management of all injuries within 36 hours.
- DCS: Rapid life-saving procedures (hemorrhage/contamination control) while deferring definitive reconstruction.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [ETC describes the defnitive management of a patient’s injuries within 36 hours... DCS describes simultaneous resuscitation with early rapid life- and limb-saving surgery.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Outline the immediate management sequence for a patient with exsanguinating external limb hemorrhage.
back:
- Apply direct pressure and packs to the wound.
- Apply a proximal tourniquet if direct pressure fails.
- Record tourniquet application time.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 376 (Book Page): [Bleeding must be controlled immediately by the application of packs and pressure... Failure to control bleeding in the limb... should be followed by the application of a tourniquet proximal to the wound.]

category: Outline management principles
front: What is the standard intravenous pharmacological protocol for Tranexamic acid in major trauma?
back:
- 1g IV loading dose over 10 minutes.
- Followed by 1g maintenance infusion over 8 hours.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [One gram is given intravenously over 10 minutes, followed by a further 1-g dose over 8 hours.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Which venous lactate thresholds guide the clinical decision between ETC and DCS?
back:
- <2 mmol/L: Likely suitable for Early Total Care.
- >5 mmol/L: Mandatory Damage Control Surgery.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 380 (Book Page): [<2 mmol/L – ETC... >5 mmol/L – DCS]

category: Outline management principles
front: What is the targeted blood product ratio in a Massive Transfusion Protocol (MTP)?
back:
- 1 unit Packed Red Cells.
- 1 unit Fresh-frozen Plasma.
- 1 unit Platelets (1:1:1 ratio).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [All hospitals managing severe trauma should have a massive transfusion protocol that aims to provide blood and blood products in a ratio of 1 packed red cells : 1 fresh-frozen plasma : 1 platelets.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Outline the presurgical management steps for an open fracture in the emergency department.
back:
- Administer immediate broad-spectrum IV antibiotics.
- Document with photography.
- Apply moist sterile saline dressings.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 444 (Book Page): [Presurgical phase... Document the severity... Apply a moist saline dressing... Administer intravenous antibiotics according to local protocols.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Identify the components of the 'triad of death' in severely traumatized patients.
back:
- Acidosis.
- Coagulopathy.
- Hypothermia.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [the ‘triad of death’ – a cycle of acidosis, coagulopathy and hypothermia – may develop and result in multiorgan failure and death.]

category: Outline management principles
front: What target neurological parameters must be maintained during the management of severe head injury?
back:
- Intracranial Pressure (ICP) <20 mmHg.
- Cerebral Perfusion Pressure (CPP) >60 mmHg.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 389 (Book Page): [ICP <20 mmHg... CPP >60 mmHg]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What is the primary survey management sequence for the initial assessment of a severely injured trauma patient?
back:
The sequence follows cABCDE:
- c: Control massive external haemorrhage
- A: Airway with cervical spine protection
- B: Breathing and ventilation
- C: Circulation and haemorrhage control
- D: Disability (neurological status)
- E: Exposure
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [Summary box 27.4 The cABCDE of trauma care: c – Control of massive external haemorrhage; A – Airway with cervical spine protection; B – Breathing and ventilation; C – Circulation and haemorrhage control; D – Disability (neurological status); E – Exposure (assess for other injuries)]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What physiological mechanism justifies Damage Control Surgery (DCS) over prolonged reconstructive procedures in unstable trauma patients?
back:
- Prevents the 'triad of death' (acidosis, coagulopathy, and hypothermia).
- Minimizes additional immune and physiological derangement caused by lengthy surgical procedures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [Prolonged procedures result in additional trauma and further immune and physiological derangement; the ‘triad of death’ – a cycle of acidosis, coagulopathy and hypothermia – may develop and result in multiorgan failure and death.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: How do management principles differ between Early Total Care (ETC) and Damage Control Surgery (DCS)?
back:
- ETC: Definitive management/fixation of all injuries within 36 hours for physiologically stable patients.
- DCS: Initial rapid life/limb-saving surgery only; defers time-consuming definitive reconstructions until physiological optimization.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [ETC describes the defnitive management of a patient’s injuries within 36 hours of injury after a period of initial resuscitation. DCS describes simultaneous resuscitation with early rapid life- and limb-saving surgery. Time-consuming defnitive surgery is deferred until the patient’s physiological status allows.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What are the primary surgical management goals for chronic osteomyelitis?
back:
- Radical excision of all infected bone (sequestrectomy)
- Management of dead space
- Bone stabilization
- Provision of healthy soft-tissue cover
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 598 (Book Page): [The operative goals are: exposure for multiple, deep bone sampling; excision of all affected tissue; intravenous antibiotics after sampling; bone stabilisation, if necessary; dead-space management; soft-tissue cover, which may include plastic surgery.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Why must loose prosthetic implants always be removed in chronic infections?
back:
- Implants harbor bacterial biofilms
- Biofilms are resistant to systemic antibiotics and immune response
- Eradication requires removal of the foreign body
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 596 (Book Page): [Bacteria can adhere to dead bone or implant surfaces, forming a complex community enveloped in a polysaccharide matrix, known as a bioflm. These bacteria... making them more resistant both to the host immune system and to antibiotics.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Differentiate the management of early versus late-presenting unstable hip dysplasia (DDH).
back:
- <6 months: Pavlik harness or splinting
- 6-24 months: Closed or open reduction (medial/anterior approach)
- >2 years: Pelvic or femoral osteotomies for reorientation
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 617 (Book Page)-618: [Up to age 4–6 months, a harness or splint is effective treatment... a medial approach open reduction can be performed between 6 and 24 months... In the older child, a pelvic osteotomy may be required to reorientate the acetabulum.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Outline the urgent management for a child with suspected septic arthritis of the hip.
back:
- Immediate joint aspiration for culture
- Formal open surgical washout (arthrotomy)
- Empiric IV antibiotics adjusted per culture results
- Joint splintage to prevent instability
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 634 (Book Page): [The treatment of a presumed septic arthritis therefore requires the prompt removal of pus from the joint and appropriate adequate antibiotic therapy. ... standard teaching states that the joint must be opened, irrigated and free drainage encouraged via the capsulotomy.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What is the standard duration and transition of antibiotic therapy for acute osteomyelitis?
back:
- 2-3 weeks total duration
- Start with high-dose IV empirically
- Transition to oral therapy based on clinical improvement and cultures
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 603 (Book Page): [Intravenous antibiotics should be converted to oral therapy, depending on clinical progress and the results of cultures, and therapy is continued for a total of 2–3 weeks.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: List the four Kocher clinical predictors used to diagnose pediatric septic arthritis.
back:
1. Fever >38.5°C
2. Inability to weight-bear
3. ESR >40 mm/h
4. White cell count >12 × 10⁹/L
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 634 (Book Page): [The clinical predictors of Kocher et al. (2004) for the diagnosis of septic arthritis: History of fever >38.5°C, Non-weight-bearing, Erythrocyte sedimentation rate >40 mm/h, White cell count >12 × 10 9 /L]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Under what conditions is the DAIR strategy appropriate for prosthetic joint infections?
back:
- Implant is firmly fixed (not loose)
- Early presentation (usually <3 months post-op)
- Requires modular component exchange and long-term suppressive antibiotics
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 602 (Book Page): [Debridement, antibiotics and implant retention - ‘DAIR’. This can only be undertaken if the prosthesis is well fxed. ... all infected soft tissue and necrotic bone must be fully excised and modular components exchanged.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Contrast surgical management of stable versus unstable unhealed infected fractures.
back:
- Stable: DAIR, debridement, and dead-space management
- Unstable: Hardware removal, external fixation (e.g. Ilizarov), and radical segmental excision
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 603 (Book Page): [Unhealed fracture with stable fxation... DAIR approach... Unhealed fracture with unstable fxation... implant... should be removed and replaced by an external fxator. Radical excision of the infected fracture is needed.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: How are Hueter-Volkmann and Wolff’s laws applied in DDH management?
back:
- Stable, congruous reduction restores physiological compressive forces
- This biomechanical environment stimulates acetabular growth and bone remodeling
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 609 (Book Page): [The conservative treatment... considers remodelling ability with an understanding of the Hueter–Volkmann principle and Wolf’s law: improving the biomechanical environment may reverse abnormal growth.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What are the first-line empiric antibiotics for a 1-year-old child with acute osteomyelitis?
back:
- IV Cephalosporins or Flucloxacillin (Gram-positive cover)
- Addition of Gentamicin (Gram-negative cover for neonates/infants)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 603 (Book Page): [Empirical intravenous therapy against Gram-positive organisms is given (cephalosporins or fucloxa- cillin), adding gentamicin to cover Gram-negative organisms in children under 1 year.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What are the primary initial steps for managing exsanguinating external hemorrhage in trauma?
back:
- Apply direct pressure and packs to the wound.
- Utilize haemostatic dressings to augment coagulation.
- Apply a proximal tourniquet if direct pressure fails to control limb bleeding.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 376 (Book Page): [Bleeding must be controlled immediately by the application of packs and pressure directly onto the bleeding wound and proximal artery... followed by the application of a tourniquet proximal to the wound.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What is the physiological rationale and blood pressure target for permissive hypotension in trauma?
back:
- Aim: Maintain supply to vital organs (brain, heart, kidneys).
- Target: Systolic BP 70–90 mmHg (or >90 mmHg if head injury is suspected).
- Duration: Must be time-limited until the primary source of hemorrhage is controlled.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 376 (Book Page): [The initial aim of resuscitation is to maintain the blood supply to the vital organs: the brain, heart and kidneys. For a short time, this can be achieved with a target systolic blood pressure of 70–90 mmHg, although a higher pressure of >90 mmHg should be the target if a head injury is suspected.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Contrast the role of Whole-body CT (WBCT) versus selective scanning in severe trauma management.
back:
- WBCT: Gold standard for patients with deranged physiology or signs of multiple injury; scan head to pelvis with IV contrast.
- Selective: No role in severely injured patients as it risks missing concurrent hemorrhages.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [Computed tomography (CT) from the head to pelvis with IV contrast, the so-called ‘whole-body CT’ (WBCT), is the gold standard investigation in patients with signs or symptoms of multiple injury or deranged physiology... There is no role for scanning selective body systems in the severely injured trauma patient.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: A hemodynamically unstable patient has a suspected pelvic fracture; outline the immediate stabilization principle.
back:
- Apply a pelvic binder immediately at the level of the greater trochanters.
- Do not remove until pelvic fracture is radiographically excluded.
- Avoid 'springing' the pelvis, which disrupts established clots.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [A pelvic binder should be applied to all haemodynamically unstable patients following blunt trauma and not removed until after a pelvic fracture has been excluded... Page 379 (Book Page): Mechanical testing of the pelvis in the emergency room (‘springing the pelvis’) adds no useful clinical examination and will disrupt any blood clot.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Outline the administration protocol for Tranexamic Acid (TXA) in trauma patients with significant hemorrhage.
back:
- Dose: 1g IV over 10 minutes, then 1g IV over 8 hours.
- Timing: Ideally within the first hour; never administer later than 3 hours post-injury.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [One gram is given intravenously over 10 minutes, followed by a further 1-g dose over 8 hours... ideally within the frst hour from injury; the frst dose should not be administered more than 3 hours from injury.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Which physiological indices signify a patient is successfully resuscitated and suitable for Early Total Care (ETC)?
back:
- Pulse <100/min and normal blood pressure.
- Urine output >30 mL/h.
- Normal coagulation screen and no acidosis.
- Venous lactate <2 mmol/L.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [indices are used to evaluate the response to resuscitation, including a pulse rate less than 100 per minute, normal blood pressure and respiratory rate, as well as urine output >30 mL/h... A normal lactate (<2 mmol/L) is a sign that the patient is probably resuscitated and suitable for ETC.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Outline the three primary surgical objectives of Damage Control Surgery (DCS).
back:
- Control of active surgical hemorrhage.
- Control of contamination (e.g., bowel contents).
- Rapid temporary stabilization (packing, shunting, or temporary splintage) to allow physiological recovery in ICU.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 385 (Book Page): [Damage control surgery is restricted to only three goals: stopping any active surgical bleeding; controlling any contamination; restoring normal physiology.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Contrast the management principles for tension pneumothorax versus cardiac tamponade in trauma.
back:
- Tension Pneumothorax: Immediate clinical diagnosis and decompression (needle or finger thoracostomy).
- Cardiac Tamponade: Operative repair (sternotomy or thoracotomy); pericardiocentesis is NOT indicated for traumatic penetrating tamponade.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 374 (Book Page): [Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis and treatment should never be delayed by waiting for radiological confrmation. Treatment consists of immediate decompression... Page 375 (Book Page): Pericardiocentesis has no role in the management of cardiac tamponade secondary to penetrating myocardial injury.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Explain the management strategy to interrupt the traumatic 'Triad of Death'.
back:
- Prevent Hypothermia: Use warmed blankets and warmed intravenous fluids.
- Correct Acidosis: Rapidly restore tissue perfusion and oxygenation.
- Treat Coagulopathy: Administer 1:1:1 ratio of packed red cells, FFP, and platelets.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [the ‘triad of death’ – a cycle of acidosis, coagulopathy and hypothermia – may develop... Page 377 (Book Page): massive transfusion protocol that aims to provide blood and blood products in a ratio of 1 packed red cells : 1 fresh-frozen plasma : 1 platelets.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Describe the execution and goal of the Pringle maneuver in hepatic trauma.
back:
- Action: Compression of the portal triad (digitally or using a soft clamp).
- Goal: Controls arterial and portal venous inflow to reduce liver hemorrhage.
- Note: Does not control retrohepatic venous backflow.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 380 (Book Page): [The infow from the portal triad is controlled by a Pringle’s manoeuvre, with direct compression of the portal triad... This has the efect of reducing arterial and portal venous infow into the liver, although it does not control the backfow from the inferior vena cava and hepatic veins.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What are the four core principles governing the management of extremity fractures?
back:
1. Reduce: Restore anatomical or mechanical alignment.
2. Hold: Maintain alignment until union (e.g., casts, internal fixation).
3. Heal: Optimize the biological/mechanical environment for union.
4. Rehabilitate: Restore joint motion and muscle function as early as possible.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 424 (Book Page): [The treatment principles that were described for the adult are equally applicable to the child (i.e. reduce, hold, heal, rehabilitate).]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What is the physiologic principle behind 'Permissive Hypotension' in trauma resuscitation?
back: Maintaining a systolic BP of 70–90 mmHg (SBP >90 if head injury) to preserve vital organ perfusion while limiting fluid boluses to avoid clot disruption, haemodilution, and worsening coagulopathy.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 376 (Book Page): [initial aim of resuscitation is to maintain the blood supply to the vital organs... achieved with a target systolic blood pressure of 70–90 mmHg... Excessive IV crystalloid or colloid solutions should be avoided because they cause haemodilution, increase coagulopathy]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Contrast the management principles of Early Total Care (ETC) vs Damage Control Surgery (DCS).
back:
1. ETC: Definitive management/fixation of all injuries within 36 hours for stable patients.
2. DCS: Rapid life/limb-saving procedures only (e.g., packing, shunting) to stabilize unstable patients; definitive surgery is deferred until physiological optimization.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [ETC describes the defnitive management... within 36 hours... DCS describes simultaneous resuscitation with early rapid life- and limb-saving surgery. Time-consuming defnitive surgery is deferred until the patient’s physiological status allows]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: In multi-trauma management, how do venous lactate levels guide the choice between ETC and DCS?
back:
1. Lactate <2 mmol/L: Suitability for Early Total Care (ETC).
2. Lactate >3 mmol/L: Under-resuscitated; requires further resuscitation or DCS.
3. Lactate >5 mmol/L: Severe compromise; mandatory Damage Control Surgery (DCS) for urgent procedures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 380 (Book Page): [Summary box 27.6 Venous lactate is an essential marker of resuscitation ● <2 mmol/L – ETC... ● >3 mmol/L – may be under-resuscitated; should either have further resuscitation or DCS... ● >5 mmol/L – DCS]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Outline the management protocol for Tranexamic Acid (TXA) administration in major trauma.
back:
1. Dose: 1g IV over 10 minutes, followed by 1g IV over 8 hours.
2. Principle: Must be administered within 3 hours of injury.
3. Indications: Suspected significant hemorrhage (SBP <110 mmHg or Pulse >110 bpm).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [One gram is given intravenously over 10 minutes, followed by a further 1-g dose over 8 hours. ... needs to be administered as early as possible... the frst dose should not be administered more than 3 hours from injury.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What are the 'four Ps' defining the operative management principles for liver trauma?
back:
1. Pressure: Direct bimanual compression.
2. Pringle: Clamping the portal triad to control inflow.
3. Plug: Direct plugging of holes with packs or tubes.
4. Pack: Definitive surgical packing to restore anatomy and tamponade bleeding.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 401 (Book Page): [The operative management of liver injuries can be summarised as ‘the four Ps’: ● Pressure; ● Pringle; ● Plug; ● Pack.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: How is 'Absolute Stability' achieved and what is its specific management goal?
back:
1. Method: Anatomical reduction and compression (e.g., lag screws, compression plating).
2. Goal: Direct (primary) bone healing with no callus; mandatory for intra-articular fractures where callus would inhibit joint movement.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 426 (Book Page): [Absolute stability. Implies no displacement or movement... achieved by accurate anatomical reduction with compression... promotes direct (primary) bone healing. ... desirable in intra-articular fractures, where callus at the fracture site might inhibit movement.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: A child with a 'white eye' orbital blow-out fracture develops bradycardia. Principle of management?
back: Urgent surgical release of entrapment. Bradycardia, nausea, and syncope comprise the oculocardiac reflex from inferior rectus muscle entrapment; immediate intervention is required to prevent irreversible muscle necrosis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 413 (Book Page): [Inferior rectus muscle entrapment in children may present as the oculocardiac refex: a triad of bradycardia, nausea and syncope. This needs to be treated as an emergency because irreversible damage related to muscle necrosis can occur within hours.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Which physiological loop does Damage Control Surgery aim to arrest in trauma patients?
back: The 'Triad of Death': Acidosis, Coagulopathy, and Hypothermia. DCS principles limit operative time to prevent surgical procedures from exacerbating this cycle into multi-organ failure.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [Prolonged procedures result in additional trauma... the ‘triad of death’ – a cycle of acidosis, coagulopathy and hypothermia – may develop and result in multiorgan failure and death. Consequently, surgical interventions... are limited to rapid life- and limb-saving procedures]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Outline the management principles of the Ponseti method for congenital clubfoot (CTEV).
back:
1. Serial manipulation and long-leg casting shortly after birth.
2. Percutaneous Achilles tenotomy (usually required to correct equinus).
3. Maintenance with a Foot Abduction Orthosis (FAO) for up to 4 years to prevent relapse.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 626 (Book Page): [Ponseti method... series of well-moulded above-knee plaster casts... most feet lack 15° of dorsifexion and require a percutaneous Achilles tenotomy... position is maintained by a foot abduction orthosis (FAO)]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What are the primary fluid management principles for severely hypovolaemic trauma patients?
back: 1. Resuscitate using warmed blood and blood products. 2. Maintain a 1:1:1 ratio (PRBC:FFP:Platelets). 3. Limit crystalloids to maintaining blood pressure while waiting for blood. 4. Administer Tranexamic Acid as soon as possible.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [All trauma centres should have an established massive transfusion protocol; Severely hypovolaemic trauma patients should be resuscitated using blood and blood products; The only role for crystalloids in the initial management of severely hypovolaemic patients is for the administration of small quantities to maintain blood pressure while waiting for blood products to become available.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What are the physiological targets and time limitations for permissive hypotension in trauma?
back: 1. Target systolic BP: 70–90 mmHg (or >90 mmHg if head injury). 2. Maintain palpable radial pulse. 3. Limitation: Must be time-limited until the primary source of haemorrhage is surgically controlled.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 376 (Book Page): [For a short time, this can be achieved with a target systolic blood pressure of 70–90 mmHg, although a higher pressure of >90 mmHg should be the target if a head injury is suspected... the key to this approach of permissive hypotension is that it is time limited.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Contrast the management principles of Early Total Care (ETC) versus Damage Control Surgery (DCS).
back: 1. ETC: Definitive injury management within 36 hours after resuscitation. 2. DCS: Simultaneous resuscitation with rapid, life/limb-saving surgery (haemorrhage control). 3. DCS Principle: Defer time-consuming definitive reconstructions until physiology is optimized in ICU.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [ETC describes the defnitive management of a patient’s injuries within 36 hours of injury after a period of initial resuscitation; DCS describes simultaneous resuscitation with early rapid life- and limb-saving surgery. Time-consuming defnitive surgery is deferred until the patient’s physiological status allows.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Outline the initial management for a haemodynamically unstable patient with suspected blunt pelvic trauma.
back: 1. Apply a pelvic binder at the greater trochanters immediately. 2. Do not remove binder until pelvic fracture is radiographically excluded. 3. Avoid mechanical testing ('springing') of the pelvis. 4. Proceed to immediate laparotomy or angioembolisation if needed.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [A pelvic binder should be applied to all haemodynamically unstable patients following blunt trauma and not removed until after a pelvic fracture has been excluded... Any patient undergoing immediate trauma laparotomy after blunt trauma without a WBCT scan should have a pelvic binder applied.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What are the dosing and timing principles for administering Tranexamic Acid in major trauma?
back: 1. Initial Dose: 1g IV over 10 minutes. 2. Maintenance: Follow with 1g over 8 hours. 3. Timing Requirement: Administer as early as possible; do not initiate if more than 3 hours since injury.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [One gram is given intravenously over 10 minutes, followed by a further 1-g dose over 8 hours... it needs to be administered as early as possible and ideally within the frst hour from injury; the frst dose should not be administered more than 3 hours from injury.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What clinical and laboratory predictors outline the management threshold for pediatric septic arthritis?
back: 1. History of fever >38.5°C. 2. Inability to weight-bear. 3. ESR >40 mm/h. 4. White cell count >12 × 10^9/L. Presence of 4/4 predictors carries a 93% probability of sepsis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 634 (Book Page): [Table 44.17 (a) The clinical predictors... for the diagnosis of septic arthritis: History of fever >38.5°C, Non-weight-bearing, Erythrocyte sedimentation rate >40 mm/h, White cell count >12 × 10 9 /L.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Outline the immediate emergency 'presurgical' management steps for an open fracture.
back: 1. Photograph the wound and assess neurovascular status. 2. Perform gross debridement and realignment. 3. Splint the limb and apply a moist saline dressing. 4. Administer IV broad-spectrum antibiotics and tetanus prophylaxis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 444 (Book Page): [1. Take a photograph... 2. Assess neurovascular status... 3. Splint the afected limb... 4. Apply a moist saline dressing... 5. Administer intravenous antibiotics... 6. Obtain a tetanus immunisation history.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What are the management principles for a clinically diagnosed tension pneumothorax?
back: 1. Immediate decompression without waiting for radiographs. 2. Use finger thoracostomy or large-bore cannula in the 'safe triangle'. 3. Follow with intercostal chest drain insertion. 4. Administer high-flow oxygen.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 374 (Book Page): [Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis and treatment should never be delayed by waiting for radiological confrmation... Treatment consists of immediate decompression... in the safe triangle... or, in extremis, a fnger thoracostomy.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Outline the target physiological parameters for severe TBI management in neurointensive care.
back: 1. PaO2 >11 kPa and PaCO2 4.5–5.0 kPa. 2. MAP 80–90 mmHg. 3. ICP <20 mmHg. 4. CPP >60 mmHg. 5. Sodium >140 mmol/L.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 389 (Book Page): [Table 28.5 Key parameters to maintain in head-injured patients... PaCO 2 = 4.5–5.0 kPa, PaO 2 >11 kPa, MAP = 80–90 mmHg, ICP <20 mmHg, CPP >60 mmHg, [Na + ] >140 mmol/L.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What are the immediate management principles for acute extremity compartment syndrome?
back: 1. Split all constrictive casts and dressings to the skin. 2. Elevate the extremity. 3. Urgent surgical fasciotomy of all involved compartments. 4. Maintain high index of suspicion in unconscious patients.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 444 (Book Page): [Emergency treatment involves splitting casts and/or dressings to the skin and elevating the extremity. Senior input should be sought and arrangements put in place to perform defnitive treatment with fasciotomies.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the primary non-surgical intervention for early Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip (DDH)?
back: Pavlik harness or splinting. These devices obtain and maintain reduction with the hip in fexion and abduction, allowing for acetabular remodeling.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 617 (Book Page): [Hips that remain unstable or that are dislocated at rest are treated with harnesses or splints that obtain and maintain reduction with the hip abducted and fexed.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the pathophysiological loop of secondary brain injury in raised Intracranial Pressure (ICP)?
back: Raised ICP reduces Cerebral Perfusion Pressure (CPP), causing ischemia and hypoxia. This triggers necrosis, infammation, and further brain swelling, escalating ICP.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 381 (Book Page): [Raised ICP can compromise cerebral perfusion, resulting in a cycle of secondary brain injury and swelling. ... Flow depends on cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP), which is the diference between the mean arterial pressure (MAP) and the intracranial pressure (ICP)]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Contrast the functional goals of Early Total Care (ETC) versus Damage Control Surgery (DCS).
back: ETC: Definitive fixation of all fractures within 36 hours for stable patients. DCS: Rapid, life-saving procedures (hemorrhage control, debridement) deferring definitive repair until physiology is optimized.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [ETC allows defnitive fxation of all unstable long bone, spinal and pelvic fractures within 36 hours of injury. ... DCS in the abdomen is limited to packing and control of haemorrhage, debridement and resection of devitalised tissue.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: A child presents with a non-weight-bearing limp and fever >38.5°C. What is the surgical priority?
back: Immediate joint aspiration and formal surgical washout (irrigation) to remove destructive proteases and prevent avascular necrosis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 634 (Book Page): [The treatment of a presumed septic arthritis therefore requires the prompt removal of pus from the joint and appropriate adequate antibiotic therapy. ... if pus is confrmed, a formal washout is mandatory.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the specific pharmacological intervention for hemorrhage control in trauma according to ATLS principles?
back: Tranexamic Acid (TXA). Administer 1g IV over 10 minutes, then another 1g over 8 hours. It must be given ideally within 1 hour of injury.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [One gram is given intravenously over 10 minutes, followed by a further 1-g dose over 8 hours. Tranexamic acid should be given to all trauma patients suspected to have signifcant haemorrhage.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: List the clinical criteria required to definitively confirm a Prosthetic Joint Infection (PJI).
back: Presence of a sinus tract communicating with the joint, synovial white cell count >3000/μL, or positive microbiological cultures from multiple tissue samples.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 601 (Book Page): [Infection is confrmed if there is a sinus communicating with the joint or there is a high synovial fuid WCC (>3000/μL), a positive microbiological culture.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: How is the 'DAIR' surgical approach applied to fracture-related infections?
back: Debridement, Antibiotics, and Implant Retention. Used for early, stable fractures where metalwork is kept to facilitate union while suppressive antibiotics are administered.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 603 (Book Page): [Unhealed fracture with stable fxation. ... can be managed with deep sampling, debridement of infected tissues and management of dead spaces ... after debridement, systemic antibiotics must be given to suppress infection until bone union.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: A patient presents with acute proptosis, reduced visual acuity, and pain after midface trauma. What is the emergency intervention?
back: Lateral canthotomy and cantholysis. This relieves intraocular pressure caused by retrobulbar hemorrhage to prevent permanent blindness.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 413 (Book Page): [A retrobulbar haemorrhage is an acute surgical emergency as it can lead to blindness ... preparation should be made for immediate bedside lateral canthotomy and cantholysis under LA.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What non-surgical physiological marker identifies patients under-resuscitated for definitive surgery?
back: Venous Lactate. A level >3 mmol/L suggests under-resuscitation; levels >5 mmol/L mandate Damage Control Surgery (DCS) over Early Total Care (ETC).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 380 (Book Page): [An elevated lactate (>3 mmol/L) suggests the patient is under-resuscitated and should either have a period of further resuscitation or DCS if surgery is urgent. ... >5 mmol/L – DCS.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the surgical goal when using the Ilizarov method for chronic BACH complex osteomyelitis?
back: Segmental resection of infected bone followed by distraction osteogenesis to fill the resulting defect and restore structural limb function.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 606 (Book Page): [When the infection is segmental (BACH complex) ... Curative resection must be segmental and bone stabilisation will always be required. The Ilizarov method ... is a powerful and successful technique.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What is the recommended dosing schedule for Tranexamic acid in suspected traumatic hemorrhage?
back:
- One gram given intravenously over 10 minutes.
- Followed by a further 1g dose infused over 8 hours.
- Must be administered within 3 hours of injury.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [One gram is given intravenously over 10 minutes, followed by a further 1-g dose over 8 hours. ...the frst dose should not be administered more than 3 hours from injury.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What are the target blood pressure parameters for the principle of permissive hypotension?
back:
- Target systolic blood pressure of 70–90 mmHg for a short time.
- Target systolic blood pressure >90 mmHg if head injury is suspected.
- Use small boluses (e.g., 250 mL) of blood or saline.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 376 (Book Page): [For a short time, this can be achieved with a target systolic blood pressure of 70–90 mmHg, although a higher pressure of >90 mmHg should be the target if a head injury is suspected.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Distinguish between management principles of Early Total Care (ETC) and Damage Control Surgery (DCS).
back:
- ETC: Definitive injury management within 36 hours after initial resuscitation.
- DCS: Early rapid life/limb-saving surgery simultaneous with resuscitation.
- DCS: Defers time-consuming definitive surgery until physiological status stabilizes.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [ETC describes the defnitive management of a patient’s injuries within 36 hours of injury... DCS describes simultaneous resuscitation with early rapid life- and limb-saving surgery. Time-consuming defnitive surgery is deferred.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Outline the immediate management steps for a clinical diagnosis of tension pneumothorax.
back:
- Perform immediate decompression in the 'safe triangle' or via large-bore cannula.
- Do not wait for radiological confirmation.
- Follow with rapid insertion of an intercostal chest drain.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 376 (Book Page): [Life-threatening chest pathology such as tension pneumothorax... should be diagnosed and managed immediately. ...Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis and treatment should never be delayed by waiting for radiological confrmation.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What product ratios are utilized in a standard Massive Transfusion Protocol (MTP)?
back:
- 1 unit of Packed Red Cells.
- 1 unit of Fresh-Frozen Plasma.
- 1 unit of Platelets.
- Use warmed blood and products to prevent hypothermia.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [All hospitals managing severe trauma should have a massive transfusion protocol that aims to provide blood and blood products in a ratio of 1 packed red cells : 1 fresh-frozen plasma : 1 platelets.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What is the gold standard investigation for adult blunt trauma patients with multiple injuries?
back:
- Whole-body Computed Tomography (WBCT).
- Must include contrast and cover head to pelvis.
- Performed as early as possible during the resuscitation phase.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [Computed tomography (CT) from the head to pelvis with IV contrast, the so-called ‘whole-body CT’ (WBCT), is the gold standard investigation in patients with signs or symptoms of multiple injury.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: Outline the emergency management principle for suspected acute traumatic retrobulbar hemorrhage.
back:
- Immediate bedside lateral canthotomy and cantholysis.
- Administer medical therapy: Mannitol, acetazolamide, and steroids.
- Goal: Urgent reduction of intraorbital pressure to prevent blindness.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 413 (Book Page): [If this is suspected, preparation should be made for immediate bedside lateral canthotomy and cantholysis under LA... Concomitant medical management should also be initiated with mannitol, acetazolamide and steroids.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What drainage volumes indicate the need for urgent thoracotomy in massive hemothorax?
back:
- Initial drainage exceeding 1500 mL of blood.
- Ongoing blood loss greater than 200 mL/hour over 3–4 hours.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 375 (Book Page): [Initial drainage of more than 1500 mL of blood or ongoing haemorrhage of more than 200 mL/h over 3–4 hours is generally considered an indication for urgent thoracotomy.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: How is venous lactate used to stage resuscitation and surgical suitability?
back:
- <2 mmol/L: resuscitated and suitable for Early Total Care (ETC).
- 2–3 mmol/L: Monitor trend (upward or downward).
- >3 mmol/L: Under-resuscitated; requires further resuscitation or DCS.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [A normal lactate (<2 mmol/L) is a sign that the patient is probably resuscitated and suitable for ETC. An elevated lactate (>3 mmol/L) suggests the patient is under-resuscitated and should either have a period of further resuscitation or DCS.]

category: Outline management principles
front: Q: What is the initial management for hemodynamically unstable patients following blunt pelvic trauma?
back:
- Application of a pelvic binder at the level of the greater trochanters.
- Avoid 'springing the pelvis' mechanically.
- Do not remove binder until pelvic fracture is radiographically excluded.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 376 (Book Page): [A pelvic binder should be applied to all haemodynamically unstable patients following blunt trauma and not removed until after a pelvic fracture has been excluded.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the primary functional advantage of Early Total Care (ETC) in musculoskeletal trauma?
back: Definitive fixation within 36 hours facilitates nursing, allows early mobilization, and reduces pulmonary complications and ICU length of stay.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [For musculoskeletal injuries, ETC allows defnitive fxation of all unstable long bone, spinal and pelvic fractures within 36 hours of injury. This facilitates nursing care, allows early mobilisation of the patient and reduces pulmonary complications and length of stay on intensive care.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: How does permissive hypotension balance vital organ perfusion with the risk of coagulopathy?
back: Maintains a systolic BP of 70–90 mmHg to limit blood loss while preventing haemodilution caused by excessive IV crystalloids.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 376 (Book Page): [For a short time, this can be achieved with a target systolic blood pressure of 70–90 mmHg... Excessive IV crystalloid or colloid solutions should be avoided because they cause haemodilution, increase coagulopathy.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Distinguish the role of Damage Control Surgery (DCS) from Early Total Care (ETC).
back: DCS: Rapid, life-saving surgery for physiologically unstable patients. ETC: Definitive management within 36 hours for resuscitated, stable patients.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [DCS describes simultaneous resuscitation with early rapid life- and limb-saving surgery. Time-consuming defnitive surgery is deferred... ETC describes the defnitive management of a patient’s injuries within 36 hours.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Why is anatomical reduction essential for intra-articular fractures to ensure long-term joint function?
back: Restores perfect joint congruity to enable normal movement and prevent secondary degenerative joint disease (osteoarthritis).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 424 (Book Page): [In general, fractures involving the articular joint surface need to be reduced perfectly back to their original anatomical position, to restore normal joint movement in the short term and avoid degenerative joint disease in the long term.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the role of Tranexamic acid in reducing mortality during major trauma resuscitation?
back: Functions as an antifibrinolytic to reduce risk of mortality from significant haemorrhage in both blunt and penetrating trauma.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [Tranexamic acid is an antifbrinolytic drug that reduces the risk of mortality from bleeding in both blunt and penetrating trauma.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Which physiological marker confirms a patient is suitably resuscitated to undergo definitive surgical reconstruction?
back: Venous lactate < 2 mmol/L; levels > 5 mmol/L necessitate Damage Control Surgery instead of definitive care.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [A normal lactate (<2 mmol/L) is a sign that the patient is probably resuscitated and suitable for ETC.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: How does the Ponseti method improve function and avoid stiffness in congenital clubfoot?
back: Uses serial manipulation and casting followed by Achilles tenotomy; avoids formal surgery which typically results in stiffer, more painful feet.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 626 (Book Page): [The Ponseti method corrects foot deformity in 95% of idiopathic cases without the need for a formal surgical release... Feet treated with the Ponseti method are less stif.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: When should surgical intervention be chosen over non-operative bracing for humeral shaft fractures?
back: Indicated for displaced intra-articular fractures, non-union, multiple injuries, or fractures that cannot be held in acceptable alignment by bracing.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 435 (Book Page): [Internal fxation is indicated for displaced intra-articular fractures, non-union or delayed union, open fractures, multiple injuries and those fractures not held in an acceptable position with brace treatment.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the mechanism of using Botulinum toxin in the multi-disciplinary care of cerebral palsy?
back: Provides a temporary focal reduction in tone to allow stretching and strengthening, improving gait and preventing fixed contractures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 632 (Book Page): [botulinum toxin allow a focal reduction in tone... giving a ‘window’ during which the physiotherapists can stretch agonists and strengthen antagonists. It is important to diferentiate between dynamic and fxed contractures.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the primary functional goal of locked intramedullary nailing in femoral shaft fractures?
back: Allows early weight-bearing and mobilization within 24 hours, returning the patient to function much faster than traction.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 437 (Book Page): [With modern locked intramedullary implants, the patient will be up and out of bed the following day and... able to mobilise with crutches.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the primary functional objective of Early Total Care (ETC) in musculoskeletal trauma?
back: Definitive fixation of all unstable long bone, spinal, and pelvic fractures within 36 hours. It facilitates nursing care, allows early mobilisation, and reduces pulmonary complications.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): For musculoskeletal injuries, ETC allows defnitive fxation of all unstable long bone, spinal and pelvic fractures within 36 hours of injury. This facilitates nursing care, allows early mobilisation of the patient and reduces pulmonary complications

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
coreConcept: Damage Control Surgery vs Early Total Care
front: Q: Why is Damage Control Surgery (DCS) utilized instead of definitive reconstruction in physiologically impaired patients?
back: Lengthy procedures cause the "triad of death" (acidosis, coagulopathy, hypothermia). DCS limits intervention to rapid life-saving steps, deferring reconstruction until physiology is optimized.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): Prolonged procedures result in additional trauma and further immune and physiological derangement; the ‘triad of death’ – a cycle of acidosis, coagulopathy and hypothermia – may develop... Consequently, surgical interventions... are limited to rapid life- and limb-saving procedures

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: How does cyclical bisphosphonate therapy improve function in patients with Osteogenesis Imperfecta?
back: It decreases bone resorption and turnover, reducing bone pain and fracture rates. This promotes weight-bearing mobility and improves overall bone strength.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 615 (Book Page): Cyclical bisphosphonate treatment decreases bone resorption and turnover. This reduces bone pain and the fracture rate, promoting weight-bearing mobility and bone strength

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the success rate of the non-surgical Ponseti method for idiopathic club foot?
back: It achieves correction in 95% of cases without major surgery. Success relies on serial casting, Achilles tenotomy, and long-term maintenance with a foot abduction orthosis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 626 (Book Page): The Ponseti method corrects foot deformity in 95% of idiopathic cases without the need for a formal surgical release... The FAO is worn... for up to 4 years.

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: When is bracing indicated in the management of Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis?
back: Bracing is indicated for progressive curves between 25° and 40° Cobb angle to prevent further deformity and avoid the need for surgical spinal fusion.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 629 (Book Page): Curves <20° do not need treatment, progressive curves of 25–40° may be braced and those >40° are considered for surgery, which involves instrumenting and fusing the spine

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Why is arthroplasty preferred over fixation for displaced intracapsular hip fractures in the elderly?
back: It eliminates the high risks of avascular necrosis and non-union. It allows for immediate full weight-bearing and rapid restoration of mobility.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 437 (Book Page): In the elderly... the head may be sacrifced and replaced with a prosthetic head... [Page 443 (Book Page)] Arthroplasty in suitable patients bypasses the problems of blood supply and weak bone and allows early full weight-bearing and return to function

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
coreConcept: Emergency Vascular Salvage in Pediatric Trauma
front: Q: What is the role of surgery in pediatric supracondylar humeral fractures with a 'white pulseless hand'?
back: It is a surgical emergency. Immediate anatomical reduction is required to restore circulation; if the pulse fails to return, vascular exploration is mandatory.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 441 (Book Page): The white pulseless hand is a surgical emergency and requires immediate attention, assessment and urgent reduction. If the pulse does not return with reduction, then the vessels should be explored

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Which nerve injury classification requires surgical intervention due to the loss of sheath continuity?
back: Neurotmesis. Because the nerve, sheath, and fiber are completely divided, spontaneous recovery is poor without surgical repair to restore the endoneurial tube.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): Neurotmesis – complete division of the nerve, nerve sheath and nerve fbre. Functionally poor outcome without surgical intervention to restore continuity of the nerve sheath.

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the objective of non-surgical 'position of comfort' and analgesia in Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease?
back: To maintain maximum joint range of motion. This minimizes permanent femoral head deformity (flattening) and reduces the risk of secondary acetabular dysplasia.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 620 (Book Page): Treatment aims to minimise femoral head deformity and the risk of secondary acetabular dysplasia by maintaining a good range of joint movement with analgesia and physiotherapy.

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: How does the timing of rehabilitation affect functional outcomes after extremity fracture treatment?
back: Rehab should start as soon as feasible. Early movement of affected and adjacent joints prevents "plaster disease" (joint stiffness and muscle wasting) regardless of bone union status.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 430 (Book Page): Rehabilitation begins as soon as feasible. It is often not necessary to wait until bone union before beginning rehabilitation... limiting global stifness and wasting of the muscles

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: How does Early Total Care (ETC) within 36 hours improve functional outcomes in trauma?
back: Facilitates nursing care, allows early mobilization, and reduces pulmonary complications for long bone or spinal fractures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [For musculoskeletal injuries, ETC allows defnitive fxation of all unstable long bone, spinal and pelvic fractures within 36 hours of injury. This facilitates nursing care, allows early mobilisation of the patient and reduces pulmonary complications.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What mechanism in septic arthritis necessitates urgent surgical drainage to preserve joint function?
back: Proteases from leukocytes destroy bacteria and the joint's collagen matrix, causing rapid articular cartilage destruction.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 634 (Book Page): [Pus in a joint is destructive: the proteases produced by leukocytes destroy both the bacteria and the collagen matrix of the articular cartilage.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
coreConcept: Damage Control vs. Early Total Care
front: Q: Contrast the functional goals of Damage Control Surgery (DCS) versus Early Total Care (ETC).
back: DCS focuses on rapid life/limb-saving stabilization; ETC aims for definitive anatomical repair and early mobility.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [DCS describes simultaneous resuscitation with early rapid life- and limb-saving surgery... ETC describes the defnitive management of a patient's injuries within 36 hours of injury after a period of initial resuscitation.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the definitive surgical intervention for compartment syndrome to prevent irreversible muscle loss?
back: Immediate fasciotomy to relieve compartmental pressure and restore microperfusion to ischaemic tissues.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 444 (Book Page): [Emergency treatment involves splitting casts and/or dressings to the skin and elevating the extremity... perform defnitive treatment with fasciotomies.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: How did the OVIVA trial modify pharmacological interventions for bone and joint infections?
back: Demonstrated that oral antimicrobial therapy is as effective as intravenous therapy if organisms are susceptible.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 620 (Book Page): [The recent OVIVA trial has shown that oral therapy is equally efective, providing that the organism(s) is susceptible and the patient can tolerate the chosen antibiotic.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Which non-surgical intervention is used for neonatal developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH)?
back: Pavlik harness or splints to maintain hip flexion and abduction for stable reduction and growth.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 617 (Book Page): [Hips that remain unstable or that are dislocated at rest are treated with harnesses or splints that obtain and maintain reduction with the hip abducted and fexed.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Why is the non-surgical Ponseti method preferred for idiopathic club foot (CTEV)?
back: Results in significantly less joint stiffness and better long-term pain outcomes compared to surgical release.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 626 (Book Page): [Feet treated with the Ponseti method are less stif, less likely to be painful and less subject to overcorrection than those treated surgically.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Which SCFE classification factor identifies a surgical emergency due to avascular necrosis risk?
back: Loder instability (inability to bear weight) indicates high risk of epiphyseal vessel damage, requiring urgent intervention.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 621 (Book Page): [An unstable slip is defned by Loder as one in which the patient cannot bear weight on the limb... This situation is equivalent to a displaced intracapsular femoral neck fracture... acute unstable SCFE is an emergency.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What physiological benefit is achieved via cyclical bisphosphonate therapy in osteogenesis imperfecta?
back: Decreased bone resorption, reduced bone pain, and improved weight-bearing mobility by decreasing fracture frequency.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 615 (Book Page): [Cyclical bisphosphonate treatment decreases bone resorption and turnover. This reduces bone pain and the fracture rate, promoting weight-bearing mobility and bone strength.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What non-surgical intervention effectively manages 80% of diaphyseal humeral shaft fractures?
back: Functional bracing using gravity-assisted traction, typically achieving bone union within 12 weeks.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 435 (Book Page): [Non-operative treatment with functional bracing will achieve union in an acceptable position within 12 weeks in over 80% of cases. Gravity can provide traction on the arm.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the gold standard non-surgical management for idiopathic congenital talipes equinovarus (CTEV)?
back:
The Ponseti method:
- Serial manipulation and above-knee casting.
- Percutaneous Achilles tenotomy.
- Foot abduction orthosis (FAO) maintenance.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 626 (Book Page): [The Ponseti method corrects foot deformity in 95% of idiopathic cases without the need for a formal surgical release and is the treatment of choice for all feet.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: How do compressive forces affect paediatric bone growth according to the Hueter–Volkmann principle?
back: Compressive forces inhibit growth, while tensile forces stimulate it. This principle allows non-surgical remodeling of deformities (e.g., DDH) by altering the biomechanical environment.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 609 (Book Page): [The conservative treatment of common conditions... considers remodelling ability with an understanding of the Hueter–Volkmann principle... Compressive forces inhibit growth.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Contrast the surgical goals for intra-articular versus extra-articular fracture stabilization.
back:
- Intra-articular: Anatomical reduction and absolute stability (no movement) to prevent arthritis.
- Extra-articular: Mechanical alignment (length/rotation) and relative stability to encourage callus formation.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 424 (Book Page): [Intra-articular fractures require an anatomical reduction and absolute stability... Extra-articular fractures generally require restoration of mechanical alignment... relative stability.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Why is an acute unstable Slip of Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE) treated as a surgical emergency?
back: It is equivalent to a displaced intracapsular fracture; urgent surgery (gentle repositioning and capsulotomy) is required within 24 hours to prevent avascular necrosis (AVN).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 622 (Book Page): [This situation is equivalent to a displaced intracapsular femoral neck fracture. This means that an acute unstable SCFE is an emergency. The AVN risk is considerable.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What non-surgical pharmacological intervention improves function in children with Osteogenesis Imperfecta (OI)?
back: Cyclical bisphosphonates; they decrease bone resorption, reduce pain/fracture rates, and promote weight-bearing mobility and bone strength.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 615 (Book Page): [Cyclical bisphosphonate treatment decreases bone resorption and turnover. This reduces bone pain and the fracture rate, promoting weight-bearing mobility and bone strength.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Which system classifies mobility and functional prognosis in children with Cerebral Palsy?
back: The Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS), ranging from Level I (near-normal mobility) to Level V (wheelchair-dependent).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 632 (Book Page): [The age-related Gross Motor Function Classifcation System (GMFCS) has fve categories that relate to mobility and prognosis (GMFCS I – near-normal versus GMFCS V – wheelchair based).]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the clinical role of a Thomas splint in adult femoral shaft fractures?
back: Temporary non-surgical stabilization using balanced traction to restore length and alignment, ensuring patient comfort and safety during transfer before definitive surgery.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 427 (Book Page): [Traction is often used in the treatment of femoral shaft fractures in adults as a temporary measure for comfort and to allow transfer of the patient, until defnitive fxation can be undertaken.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Distinguish the indications for single-stage vs. two-stage joint revision in Prosthetic Joint Infection (PJI).
back:
- Single-stage: Removal and reimplantation in one session for healthy soft tissues.
- Two-stage: Removal, antibiotic spacer for 6 weeks, then reimplantation; preferred for virulent or complex infections.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 602 (Book Page): [Two-stage... A new prosthesis is implanted after the course of antibiotics has been completed. Single-stage... removal and reimplantation are undertaken in the same operating session.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: How does functional bracing improve outcomes in humeral shaft fractures?
back: Uses gravity for traction and soft-tissue hydrostatic pressure for mechanical alignment, allowing early elbow range of motion while the fracture heals.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 435 (Book Page): [Non-operative treatment with functional bracing... Gravity can provide traction on the arm and in conjunction with a humeral brace helps to hold alignment and allow early range of motion.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the primary surgical objective for complex diaphyseal fractures in forearm bones?
back: Open reduction and rigid plate fixation to achieve anatomical alignment, allowing full restoration of forearm pronation and supination.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 435 (Book Page): [The forearm bones work together... to allow for forearm pronation and supination. Most fractures that involve both radius and ulna in adults require open reduction, anatomical alignment and rigid plate fxation.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the primary goal of extremity trauma management regarding patient outcomes?
back: To return the injured area to optimal function as quickly as possible and restore the patient's premorbid quality of life.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 437 (Book Page): [The goal of extremity trauma management is to return the injured area to optimal function as quickly as possible and therefore return function to the patient.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: How does non-operative functional bracing improve outcomes in extra-articular humeral shaft fractures?
back:
• Gravity provides traction for alignment.
• Allows early elbow range of motion.
• Achieves union in >80% of cases.
• Prevents shoulder stiffness via pendulum exercises.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 456 (Book Page): [Non-operative treatment with functional bracing will achieve union in an acceptable position within 12 weeks in over 80% of cases... and allow early range of motion of the elbow.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Which clinical predictors differentiate septic arthritis from transient synovitis to guide urgent intervention?
back:
• History of fever >38.5°C.
• Inability to bear weight.
• ESR >40 mm/h.
• White cell count >12 × 10⁹/L.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 656 (Book Page): [Table 44.17: History of fever >38.5°C; Non-weight-bearing; Erythrocyte sedimentation rate >40 mm/h; White cell count >12 × 10 9 /L.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What surgical strategy is required for a BACH complex segmental bone infection to restore limb function?
back:
• Segmental curative resection of dead bone.
• Bone stabilization using external fixation.
• Distraction osteogenesis (Ilizarov method) to fill defects.
• Plastic surgical free tissue transfer for cover.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 628 (Book Page): [When the infection is segmental (BACH complex)... curative resection must be segmental and bone stabilisation will always be required. The Ilizarov method... is a powerful and successful technique.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: How does cyclical bisphosphonate therapy improve physical function in children with Osteogenesis Imperfecta?
back:
• Decreases bone resorption and turnover.
• Reduces bone pain and fracture frequency.
• Promotes weight-bearing mobility and overall bone strength.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 636 (Book Page): [Cyclical bisphosphonate treatment decreases bone resorption and turnover. This reduces bone pain and the fracture rate, promoting weight-bearing mobility and bone strength.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What are the sequential manipulation steps of the Ponseti method for non-surgical clubfoot correction?
back:
1. C: Correct forefoot cavus.
2. A: Gradual abduction.
3. V: Correct hindfoot varus.
4. E: Correct hindfoot equinus (usually via percutaneous Achilles tenotomy).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 648 (Book Page): [Summary box 44.13: The standard sequence of manipulations is: C – correction of the apparent forefoot cavus... A – gradual forefoot abduction... V – correction of the hindfoot varus; E – correction of hindfoot equinus.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Why is locked intramedullary nailing the surgical preference for adult femoral shaft fractures?
back:
• Provides relative stability for indirect healing.
• Facilitates immediate post-operative mobilization (out-of-bed next day).
• Carries loads until union, reducing hospital stay and disability.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 459 (Book Page): [With modern locked intramedullary implants, the patient will be up and out of bed the following day... the implant will be able to carry the load until union, allowing earlier return to function.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Contrast the clinical indications for DAIR versus two-stage revision in prosthetic joint infection (PJI).
back:
• DAIR: Well-fixed implant, early infection, modular component exchange.
• Two-Stage: Loose implant, late/chronic infection, thorough excision of cement and spacers required before delayed reimplantation.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 624 (Book Page): [DAIR... can only be undertaken if the prosthesis is well fxed... Two-stage joint revision surgery... all cement and loose foreign material is removed... A new prosthesis is implanted after the course of antibiotics.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: How does multidisciplinary vascular optimization prevent functional loss in diabetic foot infections?
back:
• Proximal angioplasty or bypass improves distal tissue perfusion.
• Enhances healing of subsequent surgical debridements.
• Prevents extensive tissue loss and major limb amputation.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 629 (Book Page): [Proximal angioplasty or bypass surgery may improve distal vascularity to a level where infection surgery in the foot may be more successful... avoid more extensive tissue loss or later amputation.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What mechanical environment is required for primary bone healing in intra-articular fractures?
back:
• Absolute stability with zero movement at fragments.
• Anatomical reduction (cortical apposition).
• Interfragmentary compression to prevent callus formation that would block joint motion.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [Direct bone healing... happens in an environment of cortical apposition and absolute stability... desirable in intra-articular fractures, where callus... might inhibit movement.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: What is the primary overarching goal of extremity trauma management?
back: To return the injured area to optimal function as quickly as possible and restore the patient's overall quality of life.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 416 (Book Page): [The goal of extremity trauma management is to return the injured area to optimal function as quickly as possible and therefore return function to the patient.]

category: Discuss the role of surgical and non-surgical interventions in improving function and quality of life
front: Q: Why is anatomical reduction mandatory for intra-articular fractures?
back: To restore normal joint movement in the short term and prevent long-term degenerative joint disease (osteoarthritis).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 424 (Book Page): [In general, fractures involving the articular joint surface need to be reduced perfectly back to their original anatomical position, to restore normal joint movement in the short term and avoid degenerative joint disease in the long term.]
