citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 599 (Book Page): "The joint is held immobile in the ‘position of comfort’..." and Page 634 (Book Page): "The treatment of a presumed septic arthritis therefore requires the prompt removal of pus from the joint..."

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: How can a 'sympathetic effusion' lead to a misdiagnosis of septic arthritis?
back:
- Metaphyseal osteomyelitis causes a sterile reactive effusion in the adjacent joint
- Joint aspirate shows inflammation but no organisms on microscopy
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 635 (Book Page): "the differentiation between the two may be difficult and a sympathetic joint effusion may occur with metaphyseal osteomyelitis. Thus, if there are no organisms seen on microscopy of a joint aspirate, the possibility of a coexisting osteomyelitis must be considered."

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: Which specific pathogen is associated with septic arthritis in children with sickle cell disease?
back: - Salmonella species
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 597 (Book Page): "Salmonella spp. (particularly associated with sickle cell disease)"

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: Identify the most common causative organism of acute septic arthritis across all age groups.
back: - Staphylococcus aureus
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 634 (Book Page): "The most frequently identified organism is Staphylococcus aureus."

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: What is the gold standard investigation for a severely injured adult blunt trauma patient?
back: Whole-body CT (WBCT) from head to pelvis with IV contrast. It should be obtained as early as possible during resuscitation.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): Computed tomography (CT) from the head to pelvis with IV contrast, the so-called ‘whole-body CT’ (WBCT), is the gold standard investigation in patients with signs or symptoms of multiple injury or deranged physiology

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: How does extended focused assessment with sonography for trauma (eFAST) facilitate diagnosis in torso injuries?
back:
- Detects free fluid in the abdominal cavity, paracolic gutters, and pelvis. 
- Identifies cardiac tamponade and free blood/air in the hemithoraces.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 393 (Book Page): The technique uses sonographic assessment in the chest, looking for a cardiac tamponade or free blood and air in the hemithoraces, and assessment for blood in the abdominal cavity, in the paracolic gutters, subdiaphragmatic spaces and pelvis.

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Contrast the criteria for a positive result in Diagnostic Peritoneal Lavage (DPL) versus eFAST.
back:
- DPL: Positive if >10 mL frank blood aspirated or >100,000 RBCs/μL in lavage. 
- eFAST: Typically detects >100 mL of free blood.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page)-400: eFAST is accurate at detecting >100 mL of free blood... [DPL] cannula is aspirated for blood (>10 mL is deemed as positive)... presence of >100 000 red cells/μL or >500 white cells/μL is deemed positive

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: A hemodynamically unstable blunt trauma patient requires immediate laparotomy. Identify the essential preoperative pelvic investigation.
back: An immediate pelvic radiograph (plain X-ray). This must be obtained either in the emergency department or upon arrival in the operating theatre.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): Any patient undergoing immediate trauma laparotomy after blunt trauma without a WBCT scan... should have an immediate pelvic radiograph either in the emergency department or as they arrive in the operating theatre

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Specify the volume and method of contrast administration required to diagnose bladder rupture during CT.
back: A minimum of 300 mL of contrast must be instilled into the bladder via a urethral catheter (CT cystogram).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 403 (Book Page): For assessment of bladder injury a cystogram should be performed at the time of CT. A minimum of 300 mL of contrast is instilled into the bladder via a urethral catheter.

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Which imaging modality is most sensitive for diagnosing Diffuse Axonal Injury (DAI)?
back: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). It is superior to CT for identifying hemorrhagic foci in the corpus callosum and brainstem.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 389 (Book Page): Magnetic resonance imaging is more sensitive and is employed to evaluate for diffuse axonal injury in patients who fail to improve neurologically.

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: How is a suspected traumatic oesophageal injury definitively investigated?
back: A combination of computed tomography (CT) with oral contrast and oesophagoscopy.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 398 (Book Page): A combination of CT with oral contrast and oesophagoscopy confrms the diagnosis in the great majority of cases.

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: A trauma patient presents with severe subcutaneous emphysema and a persistent air leak. Identify the diagnostic gold standard.
back: Bronchoscopy. It confirms tracheobronchial disruption when the lung fails to re-expand despite chest drainage.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 397 (Book Page): Severe subcutaneous emphysema with respiratory compromise can suggest tracheobronchial disruption. A chest drain... will reveal a large air leak... Bronchoscopy is diagnostic.

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Interpret a venous lactate level of >3 mmol/L in the context of major trauma resuscitation.
back: Suggests under-resuscitation. The patient requires further resuscitation or Damage Control Surgery (DCS) rather than Early Total Care (ETC).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): An elevated lactate (>3 mmol/L) suggests the patient is under-resuscitated and should either have a period of further resuscitation or DCS if surgery is urgent.

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: List the primary indications for a CT head scan in infants under one year following head injury.
back:
- Suspicion of non-accidental injury. 
- First seizure. 
- GCS <15. 
- Bruise/swelling/laceration >5 cm.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 390 (Book Page): Table 28.7: NICE criteria for CT scan in children... Suspicion of NAI... First seizure... GCS <14 or <15 in under-ones... Bruise/swelling/laceration >5 cm in under-ones.

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: What is the gold standard investigation for a severely injured adult blunt trauma patient?
back:
* Whole-body CT (WBCT) from head to pelvis
* Must include intravenous (IV) contrast
* Issued as a provisional "hot report" within minutes.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [Whole-body CT (WBCT) from the head to pelvis with IV contrast is the gold standard investigation of the severely injured adult blunt trauma patient]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Which specific synovial fluid biomarkers have recently shown high accuracy for diagnosing prosthetic joint infection (PJI)?
back:
* α-defensin
* Calprotectin
* These are more accurate than traditional markers like CRP or ESR.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 617 (Book Page): [Recently, new synovial fuid markers ( α -defensin and calprotectin) have shown high accuracy in diagnosis of PJI.]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Why are both Orthopantomogram (OPT) and posteroanterior (PA) radiographs required for suspected mandibular fractures?
back:
* Provides two views at right angles (orthogonal planes)
* Prevents missing fractures obscured in a single plane
* Crucial for detecting multiple fractures (e.g., symphysis and contralateral condyle).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 408 (Book Page): [It is extremely important to have two views at right angles to each other to avoid missing any fractures.]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: According to NICE guidelines, what are the primary indications for CT head imaging within 1 hour of injury?
back:
* GCS <13 at any point
* GCS <15 at 2 hours
* Focal neurological deficit
* Suspected open, depressed, or basal skull fracture
* Post-traumatic seizure or >1 vomiting episode.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 383 (Book Page): [Table 28.3 NICE guidelines for computed tomography... Indications for CT imaging in head injury within 1 hour: GCS <13 at any point; GCS <15 at 2 hours; Focal neurological defcit; Suspected open, depressed or basal skull fracture; More than one episode of vomiting; Post-traumatic seizure]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: What laboratory criteria define a positive result from a Diagnostic Peritoneal Lavage (DPL) in torso trauma?
back:
* RBC count: >100,000/μL
* WBC count: >500/μL
* Presence of frank blood, food particles, or bile
* Raised amylase levels.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 400 (Book Page): [the presence of >100 000 red cells/μL or >500 white cells/μL is deemed positive (this is equivalent to 20 mL of free blood in the abdominal cavity), as is a raised amylase level.]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: List the four Kocher clinical predictors used to diagnose pediatric septic arthritis over transient synovitis.
back:
1. History of fever >38.5°C
2. Non-weight-bearing status
3. ESR >40 mm/h
4. White cell count >12 × 10⁹/L.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 634 (Book Page): [Table 44.17 Septic arthritis... History of fever >38.5°C, Non-weight-bearing, Erythrocyte sedimentation rate >40 mm/h, White cell count >12 × 10 9 /L]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Which three imaginary lines must be assessed on a lateral cervical spine radiograph to ensure correct sagittal alignment?
back:
* Anterior longitudinal line
* Posterior longitudinal line
* Spinolaminar line
* Disruption indicates instability or translation.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 414 (Book Page): [Assess sagittal alignment using three imaginary lines ( Figure 30.15 )... The anterior (a) , posterior (b) and spinolaminar (c) lines are useful in identifying anterior translation on lateral radiographs of the neck.]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: In Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE), why is the "frog" lateral pelvic radiograph clinically vital?
back:
* Epiphyseal displacement is often only visible on the lateral view
* Diagnosis is frequently missed if only AP radiographs are checked
* Shows posterior slipping relative to the femoral neck.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 621 (Book Page): [Displacement is often more obvious on a lateral view and the diagnosis can be missed if only the anteroposterior radiograph is checked.]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: What venous lactate level threshold indicates a trauma patient is under-resuscitated and may require Damage Control Surgery (DCS)?
back:
* Normal (<2 mmol/L): Suitable for Early Total Care (ETC)
* Elevated (>3 mmol/L): Under-resuscitated
* Critical (>5 mmol/L): Mandates DCS.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [Summary box 27.6 Venous lactate is an essential marker of resuscitation... >3 mmol/L – may be under-resuscitated; should either have further resuscitation or DCS if surgery is urgent; >5 mmol/L – DCS]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: What is the gold standard imaging modality for identifying occult fractures or soft-tissue extensions in acute osteomyelitis?
back:
* Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)
* Shows bone marrow oedema and periosteal elevation within 2-3 days
* More sensitive than plain radiographs, which may stay normal for 7 days.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 603 (Book Page): [In the early phase (2–3 days) radiographs may be normal but MRI will show bone oedema and periosteal elevation.]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: What is the classic clinical triad of acute septic arthritis?
back: * Sudden onset of severe localized joint pain. * Joint swelling and heat. * Systemic fever and irritability.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 634 (Book Page): [Classically, the child presents with pain, fever and a reluctance to move the joint; in the lower limb, this implies a reluctance to weight bear.]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: Why does "pseudoparalysis" occur in neonatal joint sepsis?
back: * The joint is held immobile in a "position of comfort." * Any movement of the limb causes extreme pain. * Common in neonatal hip infections.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 619 (Book Page): [The joint is held immobile in the 'position of comfort', with 'pseudoparalysis' in neonates.]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: Contrast the typical joint involvement sites for neonates versus older children.
back: * Neonates: Primarily affects the hip joint. * Children and Adults: Most frequently affects the knee joint.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 620 (Book Page): [In children and adults, the knee joint is most frequently affected, whereas in neonates it is the hip.]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: A child presents with knee pain but a normal knee examination. What is the suspected diagnosis?
back: * Septic arthritis of the hip. * Hilton’s Law: Joint nerves also supply the moving muscles. * Hip pathology frequently presents as referred knee pain.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 621 (Book Page): [Hilton's law, which states that a joint is supplied by the same nerves as the muscles that move the joint, explains why many children present with knee pain although the pathology is in the hip.]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: What factor guides empiric antibiotic selection for pediatric sepsis in neonates?
back: * Age-specific risk: Gentamicin added for children <1 year to cover Gram-negative organisms. * Clinical policy: Selection based on local prevalence (e.g., MRSA).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 624 (Book Page): [adding gentamicin to cover Gram-negative organisms in children under 1 year... Antibiotic usage is guided by local hospital policy, the source of the infection, the Gram stain]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: Identify three systemic risk factors for developing native joint septic arthritis in adults.
back: * Pre-existing arthropathy (especially Rheumatoid Arthritis). * Immunocompromise (Diabetes/HIV). * Intravenous drug abuse or central venous catheters.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 619 (Book Page): [Table 43.2: Extremes of age... underlying joint abnormality, especially rheumatoid arthritis... Immunocompromise (e.g. diabetes mellitus, HIV infection)]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: What is the pathognomonic movement restriction sign for acute joint sepsis?
back: * Reluctance to move the joint actively or passively. * Severe pain throughout the range of motion. * Results in a "pseudoparalysis" effect.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 619 (Book Page): [There is severe pain if any attempt is made to move the affected joint actively or passively.]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: Why must septic arthritis be suspected even if an adult patient is afebrile?
back: * Fever is absent in approximately one-third of septic arthritis cases. * Systemic markers (WCC/CRP) may be non-specific. * Absence of systemic signs does not rule out joint infection.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 619 (Book Page): [Fever and other systemic signs are usually present, but their absence does not rule out the diagnosis. Fever is absent in about one-third of cases.]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: What is the physiological mechanism of cartilage destruction in acute septic arthritis?
back: * Accumulation of pus and inflammatory cells. * Leukocytes release destructive proteases. * Proteases degrade the bacteria and the cartilage collagen matrix.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 634 (Book Page): [Pus in a joint is destructive: the proteases produced by leukocytes destroy both the bacteria and the collagen matrix of the articular cartilage.]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: Which organism has largely replaced H. influenzae as a common cause of pediatric joint sepsis?
back: * Kingella kingae (especially in vaccinated regions). * Staphylococcus aureus remains the most frequent overall pathogen.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 634 (Book Page): [The Haemophilus infuenzae type B (Hib) vaccine has essentially eliminated H. infuenzae as a cause of infection, but in some countries Kingella kingae has taken its place.]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: What is the gold standard investigation for a severely injured adult blunt trauma patient?
back: Whole-body CT (WBCT) from head to pelvis with intravenous contrast.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): Computed tomography (CT) from the head to pelvis with IV contrast, the so-called ‘whole-body CT’ (WBCT), is the gold standard investigation in patients with signs or symptoms of multiple injury or deranged physiology.

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Which investigation is required to confirm a suspected traumatic thoracic aortic disruption?
back: Contrast-enhanced CT scan of the mediastinum.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 397 (Book Page): The diagnosis is confrmed by a CT scan of the mediastinum.

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Which imaging modality is most sensitive for evaluating Diffuse Axonal Injury (DAI)?
back: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 389 (Book Page): Magnetic resonance imaging is more sensitive and is employed to evaluate for difuse axonal injury in patients who fail to improve neurologically.

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: A patient presents with a pelvic fracture and hematuria. Which investigation identifies the suspected urethral injury?
back: Retrograde urethrogram.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 406 (Book Page): Evidence of perineal injury or haematuria mandates radiological evaluation of the urinary tract from below upwards (retrograde urethrogram followed by cystogram...).

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: How is suspected CSF rhinorrhoea biochemically confirmed in a patient with a frontal sinus fracture?
back: Sending a fluid sample for β2 transferrin assay.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 435 (Book Page): there may be cerebrospinal fuid (CSF) rhinorrhoea, which can be confrmed by sending the fuid sample for β 2 transferrin assay.

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: State the histological threshold of neutrophils per high-powered field (HPF) diagnostic for PJI.
back: Five or more polymorphonuclear neutrophils per HPF.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 623 (Book Page): The presence of fve or more polymorphonuclear neutrophils per high-powered feld is diagnostic in fracture-related joint infections and PJIs.

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: What is the gold standard imaging modality for the accurate assessment of spinal trauma?
back: Computed tomography (CT) scanning with two-dimensional reconstruction.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 414 (Book Page): Computed tomography (CT) scanning with two-dimensional reconstruction remains the gold standard in spinal trauma.

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Which specific synovial fluid markers have shown high accuracy in diagnosing prosthetic joint infection (PJI)?
back: α-defensin and calprotectin.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 622 (Book Page): Recently, new synovial fuid markers (α-defensin and calprotectin) have shown high accuracy in diagnosis of PJI.

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Which investigation is most useful for identifying joint effusions in suspected pediatric septic arthritis?
back: Ultrasonography (Ultrasound).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 656 (Book Page): Ultrasound scans of deep joints, such as the hip, will identify joint efusions.

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: What is the recommended age window for performing an ultrasound screening scan for DDH?
back: Between 4 and 6 weeks of age.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 638 (Book Page): Screening scans should be performed between 4 and 6 weeks of age and treatment, when necessary, started by 6 weeks.

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: Outline the immediate management plan for a suspected tension pneumothorax.
back:
- Immediate decompression via finger thoracostomy or large-bore cannula in the safe triangle.
- Followed by urgent insertion of an intercostal chest drain.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 374 (Book Page): [Treatment consists of immediate decompression... in the safe triangle – defined posteriorly by latissimus dorsi, anteriorly by the lateral border of pectoralis major... followed by insertion of a chest tube]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: How is intracranial pressure (ICP) medically managed to prevent secondary brain injury?
back:
- Elevate head of bed and loosen cervical collars to improve drainage.
- Titrate sedation, maintain PaCO2 at 4.5–5.0 kPa, and ensure CPP >60 mmHg.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 368 (Book Page): [ICP can be controlled by simple measures, including raising the head of the bed and loosening the collar... Target ventilatory and circulatory parameters... PaCO2 = 4.5–5.0 kPa... CPP >60 mmHg]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: Contrast the management plans for Early Total Care (ETC) and Damage Control Surgery (DCS).
back:
- ETC: Definitive fixation of all unstable fractures within 36 hours of injury.
- DCS: Rapid life-saving procedures (hemorrhage control, debridement); defer definitive reconstruction until physiological stabilization.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): [ETC allows definitive fixation of all unstable long bone, spinal and pelvic fractures within 36 hours of injury... DCS describes simultaneous resuscitation with early rapid life- and limb-saving surgery. Time-consuming definitive surgery is deferred]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: A hypotensive patient presents with an 'open-book' pelvic fracture. Outline the immediate management.
back:
- Apply a pelvic binder at the level of the greater trochanters.
- Initiate massive transfusion protocol (1:1:1) and consider urgent angioembolisation or extraperitoneal packing.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 384 (Book Page): [Initial management requires the use of a compression binder... at the level of the greater trochanters... bleeding control can be achieved either by angioembolisation or by extraperitoneal packing]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: Outline the administration protocol for Tranexamic Acid (TXA) in severe trauma management.
back:
- 1g IV loading dose over 10 minutes.
- Followed by 1g infusion over 8 hours; must be given within 3 hours of injury.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [One gram is given intravenously over 10 minutes, followed by a further 1-g dose over 8 hours... the first dose should not be administered more than 3 hours from injury]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: Outline the standard surgical management plan for native joint septic arthritis.
back:
- Prompt surgical washout/drainage (arthroscopic or open) using Ringer’s solution.
- Targeted systemic antibiotics for 3–6 weeks following irrigation.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 600 (Book Page): [Correct immediate treatment of tamponade is operative... Standard teaching states that the joint must be opened, irrigated and free drainage encouraged... Antibiotics are usually given for 3–6 weeks]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: Describe the emergency department phase management for a Grade III open fracture.
back:
- Photograph wound and assess neurovascular status.
- Apply moist saline dressing, splint limb, and administer immediate broad-spectrum IV antibiotics.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 444 (Book Page): [Take a photograph... Apply a moist saline dressing to the wound... early administration of intravenous antibiotics is one of the most important steps]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: A child with acute osteomyelitis fails medical therapy after 72 hours. What is the next step?
back:
- Urgent surgical debridement to prevent bone destruction and sequestrum formation.
- Continue targeted IV-to-oral antibiotics based on culture results.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 603 (Book Page): [If the patient does not respond rapidly... surgery is indicated to prevent bone destruction and the onset of chronic osteomyelitis]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: Outline the multidisciplinary management plan for complex (BACH B2) chronic osteomyelitis.
back:
- Radical segmental bone excision and stabilization (e.g., Ilizarov method).
- Dead-space management (antibiotic carriers) and soft-tissue reconstruction (flaps).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 606 (Book Page): [Curative resection must be segmental and bone stabilisation will always be required. The Ilizarov method... is a powerful and successful technique in these cases]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: List the corrective management sequence used in the Ponseti method for club foot.
back:
- C: Cavus correction (elevate 1st ray).
- A-V: Abduction and Varus correction.
- E: Equinus correction (usually via percutaneous Achilles tenotomy).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 626 (Book Page): [The standard sequence of manipulations is: C – correction of... cavus... A – gradual forefoot abduction... V – correction of the hindfoot varus... E – correction of hindfoot equinus]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: What is the classic clinical presentation of native joint septic arthritis in adults?
back:
• Acute onset of a single hot, swollen, painful joint
• Joint held immobile in the "position of comfort"
• Extreme pain on both active and passive movement
• Fever (though absent in 1/3 of cases)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 599 (Book Page): [Most patients present after an acute or subacute history with a single hot, swollen, painful joint. . . The joint is held immobile in the ‘position of comfort’ . . . There is severe pain if any attempt is made to move the afected joint actively or passively.]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: Describe the physiological mechanism leading to cartilage loss in septic arthritis.
back:
• Bacterial toxins and lytic enzymes cause early cartilage damage
• Leukocyte-produced proteases destroy the bacteria and the collagen matrix
• High intra-articular pressure can cause ischaemic infarction and avascular necrosis (AVN)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 617 (Book Page): [Toxins and lytic enzymes from bacteria cause early damage to articular cartilage.] Page 634 (Book Page): [the proteases produced by leukocytes destroy both the bacteria and the collagen matrix of the articular cartilage. AVN may occur secondary to pressure efects or ischaemic infarction.]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: Contrast the most frequent sites of septic arthritis in neonates versus adults.
back:
• Neonates: Hip joint is the most frequent site
• Children and Adults: Knee joint is most frequently affected
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 599 (Book Page): [In children and adults, the knee joint is most frequently afected, whereas in neonates it is the hip.]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
coreConcept: Kocher Criteria for Paediatric Hip Pain
front: Q: Which four Kocher clinical predictors differentiate paediatric septic arthritis from transient synovitis?
back:
1. History of fever >38.5°C
2. Non-weight-bearing status
3. Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) >40 mm/h
4. White cell count (WCC) >12 × 10^9/L
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 634 (Book Page): [Four clinical predictors can diferentiate between septic arthritis and transient synovitis (Table 44.17)... History of fever >38.5°C, Non-weight-bearing, Erythrocyte sedimentation rate >40 mm/h, White cell count >12 × 10^9/L]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: What is the essential pharmacological step before starting antibiotics in a stable patient?
back:
• Aspiration of synovial fluid for Gram stain and culture
• Collection of blood cultures
• Antibiotics should be delayed until samples are taken, unless the patient is in septic shock
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 634 (Book Page): [The joint is aspirated and, if pus is confrmed, a formal washout is mandatory... Antibiotic usage is guided by local hospital policy, the source of the infection, the Gram stain and, in due course, the culture and sensitivity]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: Identify the diagnostic synovial fluid leukocyte criteria for acute septic arthritis.
back:
• Total White Cell Count: 50,000–150,000 cells/mm³
• Neutrophil percentage: >90%
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 599 (Book Page): [A high WCC in joint fuid (e.g. 50–150 000 cells/mm3), with a neutrophil predominance (>90%), is characteristic of infection.]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: Which organism is the most frequently identified pathogen in native joint septic arthritis?
back: • Staphylococcus aureus (commonest across all age groups and settings)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 597 (Book Page): [Staphylococcus aureus (commonest across all settings)] Page 634 (Book Page): [The most frequently identifed organism is Staphylococcus aureus.]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: A patient with sickle cell disease presents with a hot joint; which pathogen is specific to this condition?
back: • Salmonella spp. (increased risk of haematogenous spread in sickle cell patients)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 597 (Book Page): [Salmonella spp. (particularly associated with sickle cell disease)]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: Describe the clinical presentation of septic arthritis in neonates.
back:
• "Pseudoparalysis" (joint held immobile)
• Fever and systemic signs of sepsis
• Irritability and pain on handling
• Often associated with adjacent proximal femoral osteomyelitis
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 599 (Book Page): [The joint is held immobile... with ‘pseudoparalysis’ in neonates.] Page 633 (Book Page): [Diagnosis can be difcult in the very young and in those presenting with overwhelming sepsis.]

category: Identify the clinical features of acute septic arthritis in children and adults
front: Q: Which bacterium is a common cause of septic arthritis specifically in children under 4 years?
back: • Kingella kingae (often replaces H. influenzae in vaccinated populations)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 597 (Book Page): [Kingella kingae: Common cause of septic arthritis in children under 4 years] Page 634 (Book Page): [The Haemophilus infuenzae type B (Hib) vaccine has essentially eliminated H. infuenzae... in some countries Kingella kingae has taken its place.]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: Outline the standard cABCDE sequence used in the primary survey of a trauma patient.
back:
- c: Control massive external haemorrhage.
- A: Airway with cervical spine protection.
- B: Breathing and ventilation.
- C: Circulation/haemorrhage control (pelvic binder).
- D: Disability and neurological status.
- E: Exposure and warmth maintenance.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 376 (Book Page): [The primary survey aims to identify and manage the most immediately life-threatening pathologies frst and follows cABCDE. c: Exsanguinating external haemorrhage... A: Airway with cervical spine control... B: Breathing and ventilation... C: Circulation and haemorrhage control... D: Disability and E: Exposure]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: What is the recommended blood product ratio in a trauma massive transfusion protocol?
back:
- Ratio of 1 Packed Red Cells : 1 Fresh-Frozen Plasma : 1 Platelets.
- All blood products must be warmed to prevent hypothermia.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 377 (Book Page): [All hospitals managing severe trauma should have a massive transfusion protocol that aims to provide blood and blood products in a ratio of 1 packed red cells : 1 fresh-frozen plasma : 1 platelets. These must be warmed.]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: What are the three specific surgical goals of damage control surgery (DCS)?
back:
- 1. Stop active surgical bleeding.
- 2. Control contamination (e.g., bowel contents).
- 3. Restore normal physiology (address acidosis, coagulopathy, and hypothermia).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 406 (Book Page): [Damage control surgery is restricted to only three goals: ● stopping any active surgical bleeding; ● controlling any contamination; ● restoring normal physiology.]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: List the first-line medical interventions for controlling raised intracranial pressure in head injuries.
back:
- Optimise sedation and ventilation.
- Maintain serum sodium levels (>140 mmol/L).
- Elevate head of bed and loosen cervical collar.
- Use paralysis and external ventricular drainage as adjuncts.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 390 (Book Page): [First line ICP control involves optimising sedation, ventilation and serum sodium levels... Paralysis and external ventricular CSF drainage are important adjuncts.]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: Outline the specific strategies used to control acute haemorrhage in a severe pelvic fracture.
back:
- Mechanical compression (Pelvic binder or sheet).
- External skeletal fixation.
- Extraperitoneal pelvic packing.
- Interventional angioembolisation for arterial bleeding.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 405 (Book Page): [The techniques for bleeding control (compression, packing, fxation and angioembolisation) do not exclude each other but rather may complement each other.]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: What is the management plan for treating acute native joint septic arthritis?
back:
- Immediate surgical washout (arthroscopic or open arthrotomy).
- High-dose intravenous antibiotics (minimum 3–6 weeks total).
- Joint splintage and analgesia.
- Repeated aspiration/irrigation if symptoms fail to resolve.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 600 (Book Page): [The decision to perform a surgical washout and give antibiotics should be based on the clinical picture... Management is prompt surgical joint washout, followed by 3–6 weeks of antibiotics.]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: Outline the surgical components of the 'DAIR' approach for fixed prosthetic joint infections.
back:
- Radical debridement (excision of all infected soft tissue and necrotic bone).
- Modular component exchange.
- Long-term systemic antibiotic therapy (often 6 months+).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 623 (Book Page): [Debridement, antibiotics and implant retention - ‘DAIR’... all infected soft tissue and necrotic bone must be fully excised and modular components exchanged. Following debridement, the patient is treated with long-term antibiotics]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: List the essential steps in the presurgical management phase of an open fracture.
back:
- Document injury with photograph.
- Neurovascular assessment and fracture reduction.
- Apply moist saline dressing and splint.
- Administer immediate broad-spectrum IV antibiotics and tetanus prophylaxis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 444 (Book Page): [1 Take a photograph... 2 Assess neurovascular status... and reduce the fracture... 3 splint... 4 Apply a moist saline dressing... 5 Administer intravenous antibiotics... 6 Obtain a tetanus immunisation history.]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: Outline the 'CAVE' sequence used in the Ponseti method for club foot correction.
back:
- C: Correct forefoot cavus (elevate first ray).
- A: Gradual forefoot abduction (rotate around talar head).
- V: Correct hindfoot varus.
- E: Correct hindfoot equinus (requires percutaneous Achilles tenotomy).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 647 (Book Page): [C – correction of the apparent forefoot cavus... A – gradual forefoot abduction... V – correction of the hindfoot varus... E – correction of hindfoot equinus usually follows a percutaneous Achilles tenotomy]

category: Outline the management plan
front: Q: What are the 'four Ps' used in the operative management of severe liver trauma?
back:
- Pressure: Bimanual compression of the liver.
- Pringle: Manual/clamp control of the portal triad.
- Plug: Direct plugging of penetrating holes (silicone/tubing).
- Pack: Definitive packing of the liver.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 401 (Book Page): [The operative management of liver injuries can be summarised as ‘the four Ps’: ● Pressure; ● Pringle; ● Plug; ● Pack.]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: What is the gold standard imaging investigation for diagnosing medullary bone and joint infection?
back:
- Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
- Highly sensitive and specific for delineating medullary infection and soft-tissue involvement.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 598 (Book Page): [Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanning is the investigation of choice, in the absence of metal implants. It is highly sensitive and specifc, showing all components of the disease]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Describe the sonographic measurements used to quantify acetabular coverage in the infant hip.
back:
- Alpha (α) angle.
- Morin index (percentage of femoral head covered by the acetabulum).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 617 (Book Page): [Normal hip with a high α angle and a Morin index of 50% (defned as the percentage of the femoral head covered by the acetabulum)]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Contrast the anatomical landmarks used for measuring 'real' versus 'apparent' leg length discrepancy (LLD).
back:
- Real LLD: Anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS) to medial malleolus.
- Apparent LLD: Xiphisternum to medial malleolus.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 489 (Book Page): [The frst is called ‘real’ LLD, measured ASIS to medial malleolus. The second is called ‘apparent’ LLD, measured midline, e.g. xiphisternum to medial malleolus.]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: What mandatory investigations are required for a child presenting with 'red flag' spinal symptoms?
back:
- FBC, ESR, and CRP.
- Plain radiograph.
- MRI (or other specific imaging).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 630 (Book Page): [All ‘red fag’ signs require urgent investigation with a full blood count (FBC), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), plain radiograph and MRI or other imaging.]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: How long should antibiotic therapy be paused before performing a definitive microbiological biopsy?
back:
- At least 2 weeks.
- This prevents falsely negative culture results in clinically stable patients.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 599 (Book Page): [if safe to do so, antibiotics should be stopped at least 2 weeks before biopsy or surgery.]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: According to the EBJIS criteria, what synovial fluid leukocyte count confirms prosthetic joint infection?
back:
- Leukocyte count >3000/αL.
- Additionally, PMN (neutrophil) count >80% is diagnostic.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 601 (Book Page): [Infection is confrmed if... high synovial fuid WCC (>3000/μL)... Leukocyte count >3000, PMN >80%]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: When are foot and ankle radiographs indicated according to the Ottawa Ankle Rules?
back:
- Bone tenderness at posterior margin/tip of lateral or medial malleolus.
- Tenderness at base of 5th metatarsal or navicular.
- Inability to bear weight immediately or in the clinic.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 505 (Book Page): [Bone tenderness along the distal 6 cm of the posterior margin or at the tip of the lateral/medial malleolus... Inability to bear weight at the time of the accident or at the time of examination]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Which four clinical predictors differentiate septic arthritis from transient synovitis in children?
back:
- History of fever >38.5°C.
- Non-weight-bearing.
- ESR >40 mm/h.
- White cell count >12 × 10^9/L.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 634 (Book Page): [Four clinical predictors can diferentiate between septic arthritis and transient synovitis... History of fever >38.5°C, Non-weight-bearing, Erythrocyte sedimentation rate >40 mm/h, White cell count >12 × 10 9 /L]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Describe the diagnostic protocol for suspected scaphoid fractures with normal initial radiographs.
back:
- Immobilize the wrist in a cast.
- Re-examine and repeat scaphoid view radiographs 10–14 days later.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 433 (Book Page): [The standard protocol of a suspected scaphoid fracture is to immobilise the wrist and examine again 10–14 days later. If tenderness remains, repeat the scaphoid views.]

category: Identify key diagnostic investigations
front: Q: Which specific radiographic view is critical for identifying a posterior shoulder dislocation?
back:
- Axillary view.
- Standard anteroposterior views may falsely appear normal in posterior dislocations.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 420 (Book Page): [Axillary view – true value of the axillary view shown with obvious posterior dislocation of the glenohumeral joint.]
